analysis: Examined the only change in StandaloneServer.swift: the periodic kvSweepTask (head lines 562-571) now captures self weakly and calls `await self?.retryShapeWarmups()` before `kvBudget.proactiveReclaimSweep()` on each tick. The retryShapeWarmups implementation is not in the supplied units, so what it does is unverified. Security observations from the visible code: (1) The call is made on the StandaloneServer actor, so it is serialized with other actor state. The weak capture avoids a retain cycle. The task is cancelled in finishShutdown (lines 665-667) and joined at line 689, so the loop cannot outlive shutdown. A task already inside retryShapeWarmups at cancel time would be awaited in the join, which could delay shutdown and the lifecycleState transition but is not a security regression. (2) No change to authentication, the auth token config, CORS/bind host defaults (127.0.0.1), encryption, attestation, prefix-cache storage (T-041 surfaces such as SSD tier TTL, HMAC names, scope handling), or the KV budget accounting. (3) The change does not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract or App Attest authorization (TB-002, TB-011). Remaining integration question for later passes: retryShapeWarmups, defined in another file, may do model warmups that hold the load gate or run inference on resident models. Check there that it respects isLoadingAny and the native MiMo lifecycle gates (requireNativeMiMoNewWorkAllowed), does not run during stopping, and does not touch cache data across scopes (a synthetic warmup prompt must not donate to the prefix cache under a real tenant scope). That is outside the supplied evidence, so no finding is made.
